readings.title: The Greatest Commandment
readings.subtitle: Teaching the Next Generation
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 6:1] “And this is the command, the laws and right-rulings which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has commanded, to teach <dn>את</dn> you to do in the land which you are passing over to possess, [2] so that you fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to guard <dn>את</dn> all <dn>His</dn> laws and <dn>His</dn> commands which <dn>I</dn> command you, you and your son and your grandson, all the days of your life, and that your days be prolonged. [3] “And you shall hear, O Yisra’ěl, and shall guard to do, that it might be well with you, and that you increase greatly as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers has spoken to you, in a land flowing with milk and honey. [4] “Hear, O Yisra’ěl: <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is one! [5] “And you shall love <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> with all your heart, and with all your being, and with all your might. [6] “And these Words which <dn>I</dn> am commanding you today shall be in your heart, [7] and you shall impress them upon your children, and shall speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up, [8] and shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes. [9] “And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates. [10] “And it shall be, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> brings you into the land of which <dn>He</dn> swore to your fathers, to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya‛aqoḇ, to give you great and good cities which you did not build, [11] and houses filled with all kinds of goods, which you did not fill, and wells dug which you did not dig, vineyards and olive trees which you did not plant, and you shall eat and be satisfied – [12] be on guard, lest you forget <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of bondage. [13] “Fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> and serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>Him</dn>, and swear by <dn>His</dn> Name. [14] “Do not go after other mighty ones, the mighty ones of the peoples who are all around you, [15] for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is a jealous <dn>Ěl</dn> in your midst, lest the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> burn against you, then <dn>He</dn> shall destroy you from the face of the earth. [16] “Do not try <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> as you tried <dn>Him</dn> in Massah. [17] “Diligently guard <dn>את</dn> the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>His</dn> witnesses, and <dn>His</dn> laws which <dn>He</dn> has commanded you. [18] “And you shall do what is right and good in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that it might be well with you, and you shall go in and possess <dn>את</dn> the good land of which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> swore to your fathers, [19] to drive out <dn>את</dn> all your enemies from before you, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken. [20] “When your son asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What is the meaning of the witnesses, and the laws, and the right-rulings which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> has commanded <dn>את</dn> you?’ [21] then you shall say to your son, ‘We were slaves of Pharaoh in Mitsrayim, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brought us out of Mitsrayim with a strong hand, [22] and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent signs and wonders, great and grievous, upon Mitsrayim, upon Pharaoh, and upon all his household, before our eyes. [23] And <dn>He</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> us out from there, to bring <dn>את</dn> us in, to give us <dn>את</dn> the land of which <dn>He</dn> swore to our fathers. [24] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded us to do <dn>את</dn> all these laws, to fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, for our good always, to keep us alive, as it is today. [25] And it is righteousness for us when we guard to do <dn>את</dn> all this command before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, as <dn>He</dn> has commanded us.’

readings.title: Destroying the Nations
readings.subtitle: The Chosen People
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 7:1] “When <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> brings you into the land which you go to possess, <dn>He</dn> shall also clear away many nations before you: <dn>את</dn> the Ḥittites and <dn>את</dn> the Girgashites and <dn>את</dn> the Amorites and <dn>את</dn> the Kena‛anites and <dn>את</dn> the Perizzites and <dn>את</dn> the Ḥivvites and <dn>את</dn> the Yeḇusites, seven nations greater and mightier than you. [2] “And when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> gives them over to you, you shall strike them and put them under the ban, completely. Make no covenant with them, and show them no favour. [3] “And do not intermarry with them – you do not give your daughter to his son, and you do not take his daughter for your son, [4] for he turns your sons away from following <dn>Me</dn>, to serve other mighty ones. Then the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall burn against you and promptly destroy you. [5] “But this is what you do to them: Break down their slaughter-places, and smash their pillars, and cut down their Ashěrim, and burn their carved images with fire. [6] “For you are a set-apart people to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has chosen you to be a people for <dn>Himself</dn>, a treasured possession above all the peoples on the face of the earth. [7] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did not set <dn>His</dn> love on you nor choose you because you were more numerous than any other people, for you were the least of all peoples, [8] but because of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> loving <dn>את</dn> you, and because of <dn>Him</dn> guarding <dn>את</dn> the oath which <dn>He</dn> swore to your fathers, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has brought <dn>את</dn> you out with a strong hand, and ransomed you from the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim. [9] “And you shall know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>He</dn> is <dn>Elohim</dn>, the trustworthy <dn>Ěl</dn> guarding covenant and loving-commitment for a thousand generations with those who love <dn>Him</dn>, and those who guard <dn>His</dn> commands, [10] but repaying those who hate <dn>Him</dn> to their face, to destroy them. <dn>He</dn> does not delay to do so with him who hates <dn>Him</dn>, <dn>He</dn> repays him to his face. [11] “And you shall guard <dn>את</dn> the command, and <dn>את</dn> the laws, and <dn>את</dn> the right-rulings which <dn>I</dn> command you today, to do them. [12] “And it shall be, because you hear <dn>את</dn> these right-rulings, and shall guard and do <dn>את</dn> them, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall guard with you <dn>את</dn> the covenant and <dn>את</dn> the loving-commitment which <dn>He</dn> swore to your fathers, [13] and shall love you and bless you and increase you, and shall bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land, your grain and your new wine and your oil, the increase of your cattle and the offspring of your flock, in the land of which <dn>He</dn> swore to your fathers to give you. [14] “Blessed are you above all peoples – there is not going to be a barren man or a barren woman among you or among your livestock. [15] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall turn away from you all sickness and put on you none of the evil diseases of Mitsrayim which you have known, but <dn>He</dn> shall put them on all those who hate you. [16] “And you shall consume <dn>את</dn> all the peoples whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is delivering over to you – your eye shall not pardon them. And do not serve <dn>את</dn> their mighty ones, for that is a snare to you. [17] “When you say in your heart, ‘These nations are greater than I, I am unable to drive them out,’ [18] do not be afraid of them. Remember well <dn>את</dn> what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> did to Pharaoh and to all Mitsrayim, [19] the great trials which your eyes saw, and the signs and the wonders, the strong hand and the outstretched arm, by which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> brought you out. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> does so to all the peoples of whom you are afraid. [20] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> also sends <dn>את</dn> the hornet among them until those who are left, who hide themselves from you, are destroyed. [21] “Do not be afraid of them, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, the great and awesome <dn>Ěl</dn>, is in your midst. [22] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall drive out <dn>את</dn> those nations before you, little by little. You are not allowed to destroy them at once, lest the beasts of the field become too numerous for you. [23] “But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall deliver them over to you and destroy them with a great destruction until they are consumed. [24] “And <dn>He</dn> shall give their sovereigns into your hand, and you shall destroy <dn>את</dn> their name from under the heavens. No one is going to be able to stand against you until you have destroyed <dn>את</dn> them. [25] “The carved images of their mighty ones you are to burn with fire. Do not covet the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it for yourselves, lest you be snared by it, for it is an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [26] “And do not bring an abomination into your house, lest you be accursed like it. Utterly loathe it and utterly hate it, for it is accursed.

readings.title: The Purpose of the Wilderness
readings.subtitle: Warning Against Forgetting
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 8:1] “Guard to do every command which <dn>I</dn> command you today, that you might live, and shall increase, and go in, and shall possess <dn>את</dn> the land of which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> swore to your fathers. [2] “And you shall remember <dn>את</dn> all the way which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> led you these forty years in the wilderness, to humble you, prove you, to know <dn>את</dn> what is in your heart, whether you guard <dn>His</dn> commands or not. [3] “And <dn>He</dn> humbled you, and let you suffer hunger, and fed you with manna which you did not know nor did your fathers know, to make you know that man does not live by bread alone, but by every Word that comes from the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [4] “Your garments did not wear out on you, nor did your foot swell these forty years. [5] “Thus you shall know in your heart that as a man disciplines <dn>את</dn> his son, so <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> disciplines you, [6] therefore you shall guard <dn>את</dn> the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to walk in <dn>His</dn> ways and to fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>Him</dn>. [7] “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is bringing you into a good land, a land of streams of water, of fountains and springs, that flow out of valleys and hills, [8] a land of wheat and barley, of vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey, [9] a land in which you eat bread without scarcity, in which you do not lack at all, a land whose stones are iron and out of whose hills you dig copper. [10] “And you shall eat and be satisfied, and shall bless <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> for the good land which <dn>He</dn> has given you. [11] “Be on guard, lest you forget <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> by not guarding <dn>His</dn> commands, and <dn>His</dn> right-rulings, and <dn>His</dn> laws which <dn>I</dn> command you today, [12] lest you eat and shall be satisfied, and build lovely houses and shall dwell in them, [13] and your herds and your flocks increase, and your silver and your gold are increased, and all that you have is increased, [14] that your heart then becomes lifted up, and you forget <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of bondage, [15] who led you through that great and awesome wilderness – fiery serpents and scorpions and thirst – where there was no water, who brought water for you out of the flinty rock, [16] who fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your fathers did not know, in order to humble you and to try you, to do you good in the end, [17] you then shall say in your heart, ‘My power and the strength of my hand have made for me <dn>את</dn> this wealth!’ [18] “But you shall remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, for it is <dn>He</dn> who gives you power to get wealth, in order to establish <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> covenant which <dn>He</dn> swore to your fathers, as it is today. [19] “And it shall be, if you by any means forget <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and follow other mighty ones, and serve them and bow yourself to them, <dn>I</dn> have warned you this day that you shall certainly perish. [20] “Like the nations which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is destroying before you, so you are to perish, because you did not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: Not Because of Righteousness
readings.subtitle: The Stiff-Necked People
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 9:1] “Hear, O Yisra’ěl: You are passing over <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn today, to go in to dispossess nations greater and stronger than yourself, cities great and walled up to the heavens, [2] a people great and tall, the descendants of the Anaqim, whom you know, and of whom you heard it said, ‘Who does stand before the descendants of Anaq?’ [3] “And you shall know today that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is <dn>He</dn> who is passing over before you as a consuming fire – <dn>He</dn> does destroy them and subdue them before you. So you shall dispossess them and destroy them quickly, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has said to you. [4] “Do not think in your heart, after <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has driven <dn>את</dn> them out before you, saying, ‘Because of my righteousness <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has brought me in to possess <dn>את</dn> this land.’ But it is because of the wrong of these nations that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is driving them out from before you. [5] “It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you go in to possess <dn>את</dn> their land, but because of the wrong of these nations that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> drives them out from before you, in order to establish <dn>את</dn> the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> swore to your fathers, to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya‛aqoḇ. [6] “And you shall know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is not giving you <dn>את</dn> this good land to possess it because of your righteousness, for you are a stiff-necked people.

readings.title: Moses Intercedes
readings.subtitle: The Broken Tablets
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 9:7] “Remember, do not forget <dn>את</dn> how you provoked to wrath <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in the wilderness. From the day that you came out of the land of Mitsrayim until you came to this place, you have been rebellious against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [8] “Even in Ḥorěḇ you made <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> wroth, so that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was enraged with you, to destroy <dn>את</dn> you. [9] “When I went up into the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made with you, then I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I did not eat bread nor did I drink water. [10] “Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave me <dn>את</dn> the two tablets of stone written with the finger of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and on them were all the Words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had spoken to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire in the day of the assembly. [11] “And it came to be, at the end of forty days and forty nights, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave me <dn>את</dn> the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant. [12] “Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Arise, go down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out of Mitsrayim have acted corruptly. They have quickly turned aside from the way which <dn>I</dn> commanded them, they have made themselves a moulded image.’</dq> [13] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to me, saying, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> have seen <dn>את</dn> this people, and look, they are a stiff-necked people.</dq> [14] <dq>Leave <dn>Me</dn> alone, so that <dn>I</dn> destroy them and blot out <dn>את</dn> their name from under the heavens, and make of you a nation stronger and greater than they.’</dq> [15] “So I turned and came down from the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire. And the two tablets of the covenant were in my two hands. [16] “And I looked and saw that you had sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and had made for yourselves a moulded calf! You had quickly turned aside from the way which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded you. [17] “And I took the two tablets and threw them out of my two hands and broke them before your eyes, [18] “and I fell down before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as at the first, forty days and forty nights. I did not eat bread and I did not drink water, because of all your sins which you committed in doing evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to provoke <dn>Him</dn>. [19] “For I was afraid of the displeasure and rage with which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was wroth with you, to destroy <dn>את</dn> you. But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> listened to me that time once more. [20] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was very enraged with Aharon, to destroy him, so I prayed for Aharon at that time also. [21] “And I took your sin, <dn>את</dn> the calf which you had made, and burned it with fire and crushed it and ground it very small, until it was as fine as dust. And I threw <dn>את</dn> its dust into the stream that came down from the mountain. [22] “And at Taḇ‛ěrah and at Massah and at Qiḇroth Hatta’awah you made <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> wroth. [23] “And when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent <dn>את</dn> you from Qaḏěsh Barněa, saying, <dq>‘Go up and possess <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>I</dn> have given you,’</dq> then you rebelled against <dn>את</dn> the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and you neither trusted <dn>Him</dn> nor listened to <dn>His</dn> voice. [24] “You have been rebellious against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> from the day that I knew <dn>את</dn> you. [25] “So I fell down before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>את</dn> the forty days and <dn>את</dn> forty nights, for I fell down because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said <dn>He</dn> would destroy <dn>את</dn> you. [26] “And I prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, ‘O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, do not destroy <dn>Your</dn> people and <dn>Your</dn> inheritance whom <dn>You</dn> have ransomed in <dn>Your</dn> greatness, whom <dn>You</dn> have brought out of Mitsrayim with a strong hand. [27] Remember <dn>Your</dn> servants, Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Ya‛aqoḇ. Do not look on the stubbornness of this people, or on their wrong or on their sin, [28] lest the land from which <dn>You</dn> brought us should say, “Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was not able to bring them to the land which <dn>He</dn> promised them, and because <dn>He</dn> hated them, <dn>He</dn> has brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.” [29] And they are <dn>Your</dn> people and <dn>Your</dn> inheritance, whom <dn>You</dn> brought out by <dn>Your</dn> great power and by <dn>Your</dn> outstretched arm.’
